attack.final_span:
tucked under his pocket a toothbrush and a Slinky from the National Museum of American History.
On the way to the moon, Armstrong detached the toothbrush from its box, and read an inscription. The Museum honored President Harry S. Truman, whom Truman later gave the box of brush after he had lost a tooth. The note read “Give a man a toothbrush and you feed his spirit.” Armstrong then tucked the toothbrush back whence it came.
During the return trip, Armstrong requested that Buzz Aldrin, his fellow crew member and pilot, take a thorough gaze at the moon.
